dek: The systems signals, evaluation practice, and agent behavior worth watching.

stories.title: Build telemetry exports around OpenTelemetry, not a vendor lock-in
stories.summary: OpenTelemetry's design guide makes a practical case for letting customers export logs, traces, and metrics to the backend they choose. It distinguishes software customers run themselves—where built-in instrumentation and endpoint configuration fit—from cloud platforms, which need configurable telemetry drains. Preserve correlation and semantic conventions so exported signals remain useful outside your product.
stories.takeaway: Treat portability as part of the product contract: exporting data is not enough if context and meaning disappear on the way out.

stories.title: OBI adds trace IDs to existing logs without changing the application
stories.summary: OpenTelemetry's eBPF-based OBI can annotate existing application log lines with trace context, so operators can connect a failing trace to its logs without rebuilding or redeploying the service. The rollout uses a log-shipper filter to remove placeholder lines and recommends starting with one low-risk service before expanding.
stories.takeaway: This is a low-friction bridge for legacy services—but validate the filtering carefully to avoid duplicate or malformed log records.

stories.title: Evaluator backfills turn yesterday’s production traces into today’s test set
stories.summary: Langfuse's September release lets teams apply a newly configured evaluator to past observations, choosing a time window, item cap, and sampling rate while previewing estimated LLM cost. The same update describes using a typed decision model as a judge for cheap, fast observation-level scores, while retaining LLM judges where written reasoning is useful.
stories.takeaway: Backfills make eval coverage less dependent on what the team remembered to label in advance; budget and sampling controls still matter.

stories.title: Score the whole conversation, not just isolated spans
stories.summary: Arize AX's September update treats sessions as first-class evaluation and review units: teams can annotate a conversation, queue it for human review, and preview an evaluator at session level. It also adds image-aware judge templates, so a vision evaluation can inspect the actual image rather than a textual stand-in.
stories.takeaway: Conversation-level quality often emerges across turns; span-level metrics alone can miss whether the user’s task was completed.

stories.title: The OpenTelemetry Demo now traces an agent across tools and services
stories.summary: The Demo 3.0 release adds an instrumented LangGraph ReAct agent, an MCP server, and a chat UI. Its traces follow interactions from the user-facing application through model calls, agent tool use, MCP, and downstream services; a Collector processor normalizes legacy GenAI telemetry into the official gen_ai semantic conventions.
stories.takeaway: A useful reference architecture for debugging the whole execution path—not just the model request that happened to be slow.

stories.title: Agent-as-a-Judge moves production-trace review beyond fixed span checks
stories.summary: Arize describes an agentic judge that inspects production traces, locates relevant spans, and labels issues using criteria adapted to failures observed in production. In the same update, whole-session annotations and review queues connect automated detection to human inspection of the complete interaction.
stories.takeaway: Use this as a triage aid, not an oracle: validate judge labels against human review and track false positives as the criteria evolve.
